COP1030.title: Programming Concepts I (Introductory Python; Python with Raspberry Pi)
COP1030.prerequisites: None at state level, but every carrier sets one: CGS 1100 at College of Central Florida and Palm Beach State (a first programming course there); COP 1000 at Hillsborough (unconfirmed - its catalog was unreachable) and Northwest Florida State; COP 2000 at Indian River, whose version goes on to classes, recursion and GUI programming. *** SAME COURSE AS COP 2030: SCNS equivalence is keyed to the last three digits, so COP 1030 and COP 2030 (USF, NWFSC, IRSC) transfer as one course - six public carriers in all. *** PALM BEACH STATE TEACHES IT ON A RASPBERRY PI, with sensor and robotics projects; budget for a kit. Its general Python course is COP 2047. *** Not a computer-science major's first course: it usually transfers as elective credit.

offering_notes.summary: Three public carriers of COP 1030, all at 3 credits, under three different titles; three more carry the SCNS-equivalent COP 2030 at 3 credits (USF, Northwest Florida State, Indian River). No carrier publishes total contact hours; Palm Beach State lists 3 lecture hours a week.
offering_notes.derivation: Florida's convention of 45 contact hours for a 3-credit lecture course, consistent with Palm Beach State's published 3 lecture hours per week over a 15-week term. Statewide record has no laboratory component.

offerings.title: Fundamental Programming Concepts
offerings.note: Prerequisite CGS 1100. A first programming course; sections describe it as teaching an object-oriented language such as Python. Appears in computer-information-technology and programming certificate programmes.

offerings.title: Introduction to Python Programming
offerings.note: Prerequisite COP 1000, so a second programming course here. Description and prerequisite from a third-party copy of the catalog; Hillsborough's own catalog did not answer. Confirm with the college.

offerings.title: Python with Raspberry Pi
offerings.note: Prerequisite CGS 1100. Taught on a Raspberry Pi single-board computer: setting up the Pi, writing and running Python on it, and projects with sensors and robotics toward Internet of Things devices. 3 lecture hours a week (2020-21 catalog). Palm Beach State's general Python course is a different number, COP 2047.
